events.title: Farming begins at Mehrgarh
events.description: Wheat, barley, cattle and mud-brick houses at the edge of the Bolan Pass. Dentistry is being practised here with bow drills two thousand years before the cities appear.

events.title: The Indus cities begin
events.description: Settlements along the Indus and the Ghaggar-Hakra grow into the largest urban culture of the Bronze Age, spread across a million square kilometres.

events.title: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa at their height
events.description: Grid streets, standardised fired bricks, covered drains and a public bath, with no palace and no obvious temple. Nobody has found the rulers.

events.title: The Indus script
events.description: Some four thousand short inscriptions survive, mostly on seals, and none of them has been read. The longest runs to about twenty-six signs.

events.title: Trade with Mesopotamia
events.description: Indus seals turn up in Sumerian cities and Mesopotamian texts mention a land called Meluhha. Lothal on the Gujarat coast may hold the world's oldest dock.

events.title: The water works of Dholavira
events.description: A city on a salt desert island survives on sixteen reservoirs cut into rock, catching two seasonal streams. It is engineering as the whole condition of settlement.

events.title: The Indus cities are abandoned
events.description: Weakening monsoons and a shifting river system drain the cities over a few centuries. There is no evidence of invasion, and populations drift east.

events.title: Indo-Aryan speakers arrive
events.description: Pastoral groups from Central Asia move into the northwest with horses, chariots and an early Indo-European language. Genetics has now largely settled a very long argument.

events.title: The Rigveda is composed
events.description: More than a thousand hymns to fire, storm and dawn, memorised and transmitted orally with such precision that they survive for three thousand years before being written down.

events.title: Iron and the move east
events.description: Iron tools open the forested Ganges plain to the plough. The centre of Indian life shifts from the Punjab rivers to the Doab.

events.title: The war remembered as the Mahabharata
events.description: A dynastic battle in the Kurukshetra plain becomes, over centuries of retelling, the longest poem ever composed and the frame for the Bhagavad Gita.

events.title: The varna order hardens
events.description: Ritual rank divides priests, warriors, producers and servants, and a later hymn gives it a cosmic origin. What starts as a scheme becomes a hereditary cage.

events.title: The Upanishads
events.description: A body of dialogue turns from sacrifice to the self, asking what underlies experience. It is the philosophical foundation most later Indian thought argues with.

events.title: Panini's grammar of Sanskrit
events.description: About four thousand rules describe the language completely enough that linguists still call it the earliest generative grammar of anything.

events.title: The sixteen mahajanapadas
events.description: The Ganges plain organises into sixteen states, some monarchies and some republics with assemblies. Magadha will eat the rest.

events.title: The Buddha is born at Lumbini
events.description: A prince of the Shakya clan leaves his household, and after years of ascetic practice concludes that suffering has a cause and a cure.

events.title: Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya
events.description: Under a fig tree beside the Phalgu river the Buddha works out the four noble truths and spends the next forty-five years teaching them.

events.title: Mahavira and Jainism
events.description: The twenty-fourth tirthankara teaches non-violence so thoroughly that the doctrine reaches breathing and walking. It shapes Indian ethics far beyond its own numbers.

events.title: Sushruta and early surgery
events.description: A Sanskrit compendium describes cataract removal, lithotomy and a nose reconstruction from a forehead flap that European surgeons copy in the 1790s.

events.title: Alexander reaches the Beas
events.description: The Macedonians beat Porus on the Jhelum, then refuse to march further east. The contact leaves Greek kingdoms on the northwest frontier for two centuries.

events.title: Chandragupta founds the Mauryan Empire
events.description: A young adventurer takes Magadha, then pushes to the Indus, and builds the first state to hold most of the subcontinent.

events.title: Peace with Seleucus
events.description: The Mauryans take the eastern satrapies and send five hundred war elephants back the other way. The elephants turn up at Ipsus four years later.

events.title: The Arthashastra
events.description: Kautilya's manual of statecraft is coldly practical about taxation, spies and when to break a treaty. It was lost for centuries and rediscovered in 1905.

events.title: Ashoka's war in Kalinga
events.description: A hundred thousand die and a hundred and fifty thousand are deported. The emperor's own inscription says he was sickened by it, which is not a thing conquerors usually record.

events.title: The edicts of Ashoka
events.description: Rock and pillar inscriptions across the empire preach non-violence, religious tolerance and welfare, in local languages and scripts. They are the oldest deciphered Indian writing.

events.title: Buddhism is sent abroad
events.description: Missions go to Sri Lanka, Central Asia and the Greek kingdoms. The religion becomes a transcontinental one from a state decision.

events.title: The Mauryas fall
events.description: The last emperor is killed by his own general and the empire fragments. No power holds that much of India again for five hundred years.

events.title: The Indo-Greek kingdoms
events.description: Bactrian Greeks rule the northwest and strike bilingual coins. King Menander appears in a Buddhist text debating a monk, and apparently loses.

events.title: Roman trade and the monsoon
events.description: Sailors learn to ride the monsoon straight across the Arabian Sea. Pepper, pearls and cotton go west, and so much Roman gold comes east that Pliny complains about it.

events.title: Christianity reaches the Malabar coast
events.description: Tradition puts the apostle Thomas in Kerala in 52. Whatever the truth of it, the Saint Thomas Christians are among the oldest continuous communities in the world.

events.title: The Kushans under Kanishka
events.description: A Central Asian dynasty rules from Bactria to Varanasi, sponsors Buddhism heavily, and sits astride the routes that carry it into China.

events.title: Gandharan sculpture
events.description: Buddhist stone carving in the northwest adopts Hellenistic drapery and proportion. It is the first time the Buddha is shown as a human figure at all.

events.title: The Sangam poets of the Tamil country
events.description: Some two thousand poems of love and war in Old Tamil, produced under the Chera, Chola and Pandya kings. Tamil is the oldest literary language still spoken.

events.title: The Gupta Empire founded
events.description: A dynasty out of Magadha reunites northern India and presides over three centuries in which classical Indian art, science and Sanskrit letters take their final shape.

events.title: Kalidasa
events.description: The playwright of Shakuntala and the poet of the Meghaduta becomes the standard against which Sanskrit literature is measured ever afterwards.

events.title: Faxian reports on Gupta India
events.description: A Chinese pilgrim spends six years in the country and describes free hospitals, safe roads and a government that does not require travel documents.

events.title: The Ajanta caves painted
events.description: Thirty caves cut into a river gorge carry the finest surviving ancient Indian painting. They are abandoned, forgotten, and stumbled on by a British hunting party in 1819.

events.title: Aryabhata's astronomy
events.description: At twenty-three he gives a value for pi good to four places, explains eclipses without demons, and says the earth rotates on its axis.

events.title: The decimal place value system
events.description: A written zero used as a number in its own right, with place value, makes arithmetic tractable. It reaches Europe through Arabic intermediaries and is still called Arabic numerals there.

events.title: The Huna invasions break the Guptas
events.description: White Hun incursions from the northwest are eventually repulsed, but the empire never recovers its finances or its reach.

events.title: Harsha rules the north
events.description: The last great classical northern kingdom lasts as long as its founder does, and dissolves on his death forty-one years later.

events.title: Xuanzang travels in India
events.description: The Chinese monk spends fourteen years studying at Nalanda and leaves a description of the country detailed enough to guide excavation twelve centuries later.

events.title: Nalanda at its height
events.description: A monastic university of some ten thousand students and two thousand teachers, with a nine-storey library, drawing scholars from Tibet, China, Korea and Persia.

events.title: The Arab conquest of Sindh
events.description: An Umayyad expedition takes the lower Indus. Islam arrives in India by sea and by frontier, three centuries before it arrives by army.

events.title: The tripartite struggle
events.description: Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas fight over Kanauj for two centuries. Nobody wins, and the north stays divided when the Turks arrive.

events.title: Adi Shankara
events.description: A philosopher who dies at thirty-two reorganises Hindu thought around non-dualism and founds monastic centres at the four corners of the country.

events.title: The Kailasa temple at Ellora
events.description: A full temple carved downward out of one basalt hill, some two hundred thousand tonnes of rock removed, with no possibility of correcting a mistake.

events.title: Rajaraja Chola comes to the throne
events.description: The Chola state runs a professional navy, an audited village administration and a temple economy that functions as a banking system.

events.title: The Brihadeeswarar temple completed
events.description: A granite tower over sixty metres high, built in seven years, in a region with no granite. The Cholas moved the stone fifty kilometres.

events.title: Mahmud of Ghazni sacks Somnath
events.description: The last of seventeen raids strips the temple treasury. The looting is remembered for a thousand years and is still being used politically.

events.title: Chola fleets raid Srivijaya
events.description: A naval expedition across the Bay of Bengal attacks the trading empire of Sumatra. It is the only sustained Indian projection of sea power before the modern era.

events.title: Al-Biruni's book on India
events.description: A Persian scholar learns Sanskrit and writes an account of Indian science and religion so even-handed that it is startling from the entourage of an invader.

events.title: Bhaskara II and the Lilavati
events.description: Algebra, quadratic equations and the beginnings of differential reasoning, written partly as arithmetic problems addressed to his daughter.

events.title: The second battle of Tarain
events.description: Muhammad of Ghor defeats Prithviraj Chauhan and the Rajput confederacy. Northern India passes under Turkic rule within fifteen years.

events.title: Nalanda is destroyed
events.description: Bakhtiyar Khalji's cavalry burn the monastic university. The library is said to have smouldered for months, and Indian Buddhism effectively ends.

events.title: The Delhi Sultanate founded
events.description: A Turkic slave-general takes Delhi on his master's death and founds a state that lasts three hundred and twenty years under five dynasties.

events.title: The Qutb Minar completed
events.description: A seventy-three metre victory tower in red sandstone, raised beside a mosque built from the columns of twenty-seven demolished temples.

events.title: Razia Sultana takes the throne
events.description: The only woman to rule Delhi in her own right lasts less than four years against a nobility that will not accept her.

events.title: The Mongols are held on the Indus
events.description: Repeated Mongol invasions are beaten back, largely by Alauddin Khalji. India is one of the few settled regions they never take.

events.title: Alauddin Khalji's price controls
events.description: To pay for a standing army against the Mongols, the sultan fixes the price of grain, cloth and horses and polices the markets brutally. It works while he lives.

events.title: The capital is marched to Daulatabad
events.description: Muhammad bin Tughlaq moves the entire population of Delhi eleven hundred kilometres south, then changes his mind. Many die on each journey.

events.title: Vijayanagara is founded
events.description: A southern empire rises on the Tungabhadra and holds the Deccan for two centuries. Its capital becomes one of the largest cities in the world.

events.title: Timur sacks Delhi
events.description: The city is taken, the population massacred over several days, and the Sultanate reduced to a district. Timur takes the stonemasons back to Samarkand.

events.title: Kabir
events.description: A weaver from Varanasi writes verse that attacks Hindu and Muslim orthodoxy with equal contempt, and is claimed by both after his death.

events.title: Guru Nanak is born
events.description: The founder of Sikhism preaches one God, rejects caste and ritual, and institutes a common kitchen where anyone eats beside anyone.

events.title: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut
events.description: A sea route from Europe to the pepper coast is opened. Within a decade the Portuguese are using naval force to control who may trade in the Indian Ocean.

events.title: The Portuguese take Goa
events.description: Afonso de Albuquerque seizes a base that Portugal holds for four hundred and fifty-one years, longer than any other European possession in India.

events.title: The first battle of Panipat
events.description: Babur beats a far larger Sultanate army with field artillery and mobile cavalry, and founds the Mughal dynasty.

events.title: Sher Shah Suri interrupts the Mughals
events.description: An Afghan noble drives Humayun out and in five years builds the Grand Trunk Road, a silver rupee and a land survey the Mughals simply inherit.

events.title: Akbar comes to the throne at thirteen
events.description: Forty-nine years of expansion, a land revenue system based on measured yields, and Rajput marriages that turn defeated enemies into the officer corps.

events.title: The jizya is abolished
events.description: Akbar removes the tax on non-Muslims and the pilgrim tax with it. It is reimposed a century later, and the reversal is remembered as the turn.

events.title: Fatehpur Sikri built
events.description: A new capital in red sandstone, finished in fifteen years and abandoned in fourteen more, apparently for want of water.

events.title: The battle of Haldighati
events.description: Maharana Pratap of Mewar fights the Mughals to a standstill and refuses submission for the rest of his life. He becomes the Rajput symbol of it.

events.title: The Din-i Ilahi
events.description: Akbar's synthetic court religion attracts a couple of dozen followers and dies with him, but the debates behind it are the most open in Indian courtly history.

events.title: The East India Company is chartered
events.description: Elizabeth grants a monopoly on trade east of the Cape to a syndicate of London merchants. It ends up governing a subcontinent.

events.title: The Company gets a factory at Surat
events.description: A trading post is permitted after the Company beats a Portuguese squadron offshore. The English are in as a naval power from the start.

events.title: The Taj Mahal begun
events.description: Shah Jahan builds a tomb for Mumtaz Mahal over twenty-two years. It is the high point of Mughal building and a serious drain on the treasury.

events.title: Aurangzeb takes the throne
events.description: He imprisons his father, kills his brothers, and rules for forty-nine years. The empire reaches its greatest extent and exhausts itself doing so.

events.title: Shivaji is crowned
events.description: A Maratha commander who has spent twenty years raiding the Deccan has himself formally enthroned, and founds the power that inherits Mughal India.

events.title: The jizya returns
events.description: Aurangzeb reimposes the tax on non-Muslims and orders temples demolished. It hardens Rajput, Maratha and Sikh opposition into permanent war.

events.title: The Khalsa is founded
events.description: Guru Gobind Singh initiates a martial order with its own discipline and names, after two Sikh gurus have been executed by the Mughal state.

events.title: Aurangzeb dies and the empire fractures
events.description: Within a generation the Mughals are a Delhi court with a large title. The Marathas, the Nizam, Awadh and Bengal are the real powers.

events.title: Nadir Shah sacks Delhi
events.description: The Persian ruler takes the city, kills tens of thousands, and leaves with the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor. Mughal prestige never returns.

events.title: The battle of Plassey
events.description: Robert Clive beats the Nawab of Bengal with an army a tenth the size, after buying his commander. A trading company acquires a province.

events.title: The third battle of Panipat
events.description: Ahmad Shah Durrani destroys the Maratha army in a single day. The one Indian power that might have replaced the Mughals is crippled.

events.title: The Company takes the revenues of Bengal
events.description: The diwani grants the right to collect tax from thirty million people. The Company is now a government that answers to shareholders.

events.title: The great Bengal famine of 1770
events.description: Perhaps ten million die, a third of the province, while revenue collection is enforced and grain is held for price. It is the first great scandal of Company rule.

events.title: The Asiatic Society founded
events.description: William Jones notices that Sanskrit, Greek and Latin are related, and the Indo-European family is discovered from Calcutta.

events.title: The Permanent Settlement
events.description: Bengal revenue is fixed forever with zamindars as landlords. It creates a rentier class, wrecks tenant security, and is never undone before 1947.

events.title: Tipu Sultan is killed at Seringapatam
events.description: The last serious armed resistance in the south ends. Tipu's rocket artillery is shipped to Woolwich and copied.

events.title: The Marathas are defeated
events.description: The third Anglo-Maratha war ends the confederacy. The Company is now the paramount power from Cape Comorin to the Sutlej.

events.title: Sati is banned
events.description: Widow burning is made a criminal offence after a long campaign by Ram Mohan Roy. Reform from within and reform imposed from outside arrive together.

events.title: Macaulay's minute on education
events.description: English becomes the language of instruction, to form a class Indian in blood and English in taste. It produces the professionals who later demand independence.

events.title: The Punjab is annexed
events.description: Two wars with the Sikh empire end with the Company holding the last independent Indian state of any size, and the Koh-i-Noor going to London.

events.title: The first railway
events.description: Thirty-four kilometres from Bombay to Thane. Within fifty years India has one of the largest networks in the world, laid out to move goods to ports.

events.title: The rebellion begins at Meerut
events.description: Sepoys mutiny over greased cartridges and much else, and the rising spreads across the north. Both sides commit atrocities and the reprisals go on for a year.

events.title: The Company is abolished
events.description: The Crown takes over directly, the last Mughal is exiled to Rangoon, and India is governed from Whitehall through a viceroy.

events.title: The Indian Councils Act
events.description: A handful of Indians are admitted to advisory councils with no power. It sets the pattern of concession by instalment for the next eighty years.

events.title: Famine in the Deccan
events.description: Between five and ten million die while grain is exported and relief is rationed on the theory that generosity encourages dependence.

events.title: The Indian National Congress
events.description: Seventy-two delegates meet in Bombay to petition for a larger Indian share in government. It becomes the vehicle of the independence movement.

events.title: Vivekananda in Chicago
events.description: An address to the World Parliament of Religions makes Hindu thought internationally visible and gives Indian nationalism a confidence it had lacked.

events.title: The partition of Bengal
events.description: Curzon splits the province on lines that look designed to divide Hindus and Muslims. Mass boycott of British goods follows and the partition is reversed in 1911.

events.title: The Muslim League founded
events.description: A separate political body at Dacca, initially loyal, eventually the vehicle for a separate state.

events.title: The capital moves to Delhi
events.description: The government leaves Calcutta for a purpose-built imperial city. Lutyens takes twenty years over it and it is finished sixteen years before the British leave.

events.title: Gandhi returns from South Africa
events.description: Twenty-one years of campaigning against racial laws have produced a method: mass non-violent refusal, and a willingness to go to prison for it.

events.title: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre
events.description: Troops fire on a penned crowd at Amritsar for ten minutes. Several hundred are killed at least, and Indian faith in British justice does not survive it.

events.title: Non-cooperation
events.description: Congress under Gandhi calls for boycott of courts, schools and titles. He calls it off in 1922 after a mob at Chauri Chaura burns policemen alive.

events.title: Ambedkar burns the Manusmriti
events.description: A Dalit lawyer with doctorates from Columbia and the LSE leads a march to drink from a public tank, and attacks caste as the central Indian injustice.

events.title: The Salt March
events.description: Gandhi walks three hundred and eighty-five kilometres to the sea and picks up a lump of salt. Sixty thousand are jailed and the campaign is reported worldwide.

events.title: The Government of India Act
events.description: Provincial autonomy and elections that Congress wins nearly everywhere. Much of it survives as the structure of the Indian constitution.

events.title: The Lahore Resolution
events.description: The Muslim League demands independent states in the Muslim-majority regions. Partition moves from an idea to a negotiating position.

events.title: Quit India
events.description: Congress demands immediate withdrawal and its entire leadership is jailed for the rest of the war. Meanwhile two and a half million Indians serve in the British army.

events.title: The Bengal famine of 1943
events.description: Around three million die, with wartime requisitioning, boat confiscation and refusal to divert shipping among the causes. There is no drought that year worth the name.

events.title: Direct Action Day
events.description: Four days of killing in Calcutta leave several thousand dead and make an orderly transfer of power much harder to imagine.

events.title: Independence and partition
events.description: Two states are created on a line drawn in five weeks by a man who had never been to India. Ten to twenty million are displaced and perhaps a million die.

events.title: The first war over Kashmir
events.description: The maharaja accedes to India as tribesmen from Pakistan invade. A ceasefire line in 1949 becomes a border that is still contested.

events.title: Gandhi is assassinated
events.description: A Hindu nationalist shoots him at a prayer meeting in Delhi, five months after independence, for being too conciliatory towards Muslims.

events.title: The princely states are integrated
events.description: Five hundred and sixty-two states are absorbed, mostly by negotiation, with Hyderabad taken by force in five days.

events.title: The constitution comes into force
events.description: The longest written constitution in the world, drafted under Ambedkar, abolishes untouchability and gives universal adult suffrage to a country that is largely illiterate.

events.title: The first general election
events.description: One hundred and seventy-three million voters, symbols on the ballot for those who cannot read, and six months of polling. It works.

events.title: States reorganised on language
events.description: Provincial boundaries are redrawn along linguistic lines after protest and a hunger strike death. It defuses the issue that was expected to break the country.

events.title: Goa is annexed
events.description: Indian troops end four and a half centuries of Portuguese rule in thirty-six hours.

events.title: The war with China
events.description: A month of fighting in the Himalayas ends in defeat and a unilateral Chinese withdrawal. Non-alignment loses much of its shine.

events.title: The Green Revolution
events.description: Dwarf wheat, fertiliser and tube wells turn a country importing grain under American licence into a net exporter within a decade.

events.title: The war that creates Bangladesh
events.description: India intervenes in the Pakistani civil war after ten million refugees cross the border. Ninety thousand Pakistani troops surrender in thirteen days.

events.title: The first nuclear test
events.description: A device is detonated at Pokhran and called a peaceful nuclear explosion. India is placed under technology sanctions for two decades.

events.title: The Emergency
events.description: Indira Gandhi suspends civil liberties for twenty-one months, jails the opposition and censors the press, then calls an election and loses it.

events.title: Operation Blue Star and its aftermath
events.description: The army storms the Golden Temple, and Indira Gandhi is assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards. Some three thousand Sikhs are killed in Delhi in the following days.

events.title: The Bhopal gas disaster
events.description: Methyl isocyanate leaks from a Union Carbide plant and kills thousands within days. The site is still not properly cleaned.

events.title: The economy is opened
events.description: With three weeks of reserves left, licensing is dismantled and the rupee devalued. Growth roughly doubles over the following two decades.

events.title: The Babri Masjid is demolished
events.description: A mosque at Ayodhya is pulled down by a crowd and riots follow across the country. It reshapes Indian politics along religious lines.

events.title: Nuclear tests at Pokhran
events.description: Five devices are detonated and India declares itself a nuclear weapons state. Pakistan follows within a fortnight.

events.title: The Kargil conflict
events.description: Pakistani troops occupy heights on the Indian side of the line of control and are pushed off over ten weeks. It is the first war between two nuclear states.

events.title: The software industry takes off
events.description: Bangalore and Hyderabad build a services export sector on the back of the Y2K remediation work and English-language engineering graduates.

events.title: The Mumbai attacks
events.description: Ten gunmen from Pakistan hold parts of the city for four days and kill one hundred and seventy-five people.

events.title: Mangalyaan reaches Mars
events.description: India puts an orbiter around Mars at the first attempt, for less than the budget of a Hollywood film about doing so.

events.title: Chandrayaan-3 lands near the lunar south pole
events.description: The first soft landing in that region by anyone, four years after the previous attempt crashed.

events.title: India becomes the most populous country
events.description: It passes China at about 1.43 billion people, with a median age of twenty-eight against China's thirty-nine.
